Scan 117, S117-01: the page proposes data consisting of analytic spaces, symmetric-group torsors, morphisms and Cartesian diagrams. These analytic construction assertions are carried as background; the existence or equivalence of the full analytic structure was not proved from this page.

Scan 117, S117-02: a limited finite-fibre check was actually performed. For a d-element set I, the sets of 0-element and d-element subsets each have one element, and the set of 1-element subsets has d elements. Under the stated interpretation of P_r(I_d), this supports the fibre counts in the upper margin. It does not itself establish analytic isomorphisms or analytic covering properties of the displayed spaces.

Scan 117, S117-03: a limited finite-set check was actually performed for the tautological construction. Choosing a d'-element subset A of I and then a d''-element subset B of A is exactly choosing a flag B subset A subset I with those cardinalities. The forward and inverse correspondences are literal inclusion/forgetful assignments and commute with permutations of I. This checks the nested-subset fibre model behind the NB note, not the analytic descent of the spaces or every written index.

Scan 117, S117-04: Cartesianity of (175) and (176) is a manuscript assertion/construction condition carried as background. The visible high clusters on two d indices remain unresolved. Blind audit B15 resolved the lower group base to D_{d,d'} with one prime; no global re-proof of these squares was claimed.

The product in the first live associated-cover formula is a cross, whereas the later definition uses a wedge. Both group labels are below their operator. These literal signs and placements are preserved even if a uniform contracted-product convention might be expected.
